Un horror che vuole sembrare qualcosa di grande o filosofico, ma fallisce miseramente proponendo un film che non ha senso. Il film, per quanto possa partire discretamente, è abbastanza blando. Tutto sembra essere costruito in funzione di uno scopo finale, ovvero la morte dei protagonisti. Quello che viene raccontato è abbastanza prevedibile e i personaggi compiono continuamente azioni che non hanno senso logico. Molte volte avrebbero potuto fare altre cose che li avrebbero eventualmente salvati, ma non l’hanno fatto. Il fatto che continuino a fidarsi non ha senso e il finale è qualcosa di insensato e che sembra essere dovuto, a causa delle loro continue decisioni. L’unica, forse, cosa positiva è la frase finale, quando viene detto “me l’avete lasciato fare”. Quella roba lì è vera, appunto, ci sta, però ha senso solo perché è stata una decisione della narrazione. Fanno costantemente azioni che non hanno senso, è ovvio che gliel’hanno lasciato fare. Avrebbero potuto scappare 1000 volte e nonostante questo non l’hanno fatto, hanno avuto 1000 occasioni, e c’è gente che cerca di trovarci un significato, manco fosse un film psicologico pieno di plot twist, quando è solo una porcheria, con una scrittura degna di un film dell’Asylum. Non riesco veramente a capire la gente che dice di essersi spaventata e di aver avuto una tensione assieme a un’ansia costante, non c’è un singolo momento di paura, arriva un pizzico di tensione forse verso la fine del film, ma anche lì era talmente prevedibile che a me veniva da ridere. Un altro problema che ho trovato è nella sceneggiatura, perché non è soltanto il comportamento dei personaggi a risultare poco convincente, ma proprio il modo in cui la storia viene costruita. Si percepisce troppo che determinati avvenimenti debbano necessariamente accadere per arrivare alla conclusione che il film si è prefissato, invece di sembrare una conseguenza naturale di quello che è successo prima. Questo rende anche difficile prendere sul serio quello che sta succedendo, perché più la storia va avanti e più sembra che siano le esigenze della sceneggiatura a guidare i personaggi. Anche il ritmo non mi ha convinto particolarmente. Il film cerca di creare tensione attraverso l’attesa e attraverso alcune situazioni ambigue, ma personalmente non ho trovato questa tensione particolarmente efficace. Alcune parti mi sono sembrate semplicemente dilatate, senza che questo aggiungesse davvero qualcosa alla storia o rendesse la situazione più inquietante. Forse ho apprezzato un po’ la fotografia, assieme ad alcune inquadrature, ma diciamo che più che apprezzabili, sono il minimo indispensabile. Alla fine, quindi, più che paura o inquietudine, mi è rimasta soprattutto una sensazione di vuoto. Il film vorrebbe arrivare a un finale scioccante e lasciare qualcosa allo spettatore, ma per me il percorso necessario per arrivarci è talmente poco convincente che, invece di rimanere colpito da quello che succede, finisco per distaccarmi completamente dalla storia.

May that movie’s watered-down ending dilute the original intent behind the plot, so be it. But it undoubtedly poses a version of an ending I wish to come out of a story of that kind. While I thoroughly enjoyed this Danish original’s first two acts, everything just crumbled at a certain point. Movies purely opting for shock value with their relentless bleakness tend to fall apart for me more often than not. The reason for that being that so often in those films, you have to forgive countless unreasonable character decisions in order to make the plot work. And this arguably marks one of the most criminal offenders of that I have ever witnessed. I’ll thankfully take the James McAvoy version over this any day of the week.

SPOILER ! Bu film; bir önceki review'daki filmin orijinal Danimarka versiyonuydu. İzledim şimdi. Pek sevmedim. Bazı ufak tefek olaylar dışında 2 film de tamamen farklı denebilir. Konular aynı fakat gidişat farklı. Ve bu film çok travmatik, acılı, korkunç ve çok kötü bir sonla bitiyor. Diğer film mutlu son ile bitiyordu. ----------------------------------------------------------- Bu film de aynı şekilde sosyal nezaketin, "ayıp olmasın diye" kültürünün insanı nerelere sürükleyebileceğini gösteren, izleyiciyi psikolojik olarak etkileyen bir yapım. Fakat ben şahsen, James McAvoy'un başrolünde olduğu 2024 Hollywood uyarlamasını kesinlikle çok daha fazla sevdim ve daha başarılı buldum. ----------------------------------------------------------- Çünkü bu orijinal filmdeki kurban çiftin pasifliği ve ezikliği, bir noktadan sonra beni germekten ziyade inanılmaz derecede sinirlendirdi. Evet, film modern insanın çatışmadan kaçma acizliğini anlatmaya çalışıyor; bunu anlıyorum. Ama bir anne ve babanın, çocuklarının gözünün önünde dilsiz bırakılmasına ve kendilerinin taşlanarak öldürüldükleri kısma kadar asla en ufak bir fiziksel direnç bile göstermemesi, bana "sosyal eleştiri" sınırlarını aşıp tamamen saçma bir teslimiyet gibi geldi. ----------------------------------------------------------- 2024 versiyonu ise bu hikayeyi çok daha dinamik ve izlenebilir bir boyuta taşımış. Amerikalı aile de ilk başta kibarlık budalası gibi davranıyor, sınırlarının aşılmasına göz yumuyor; yani orijinal filmin tekinsiz, pasif-agresif gerilim atmosferini ilk 2 perdede yine sonuna kadar hissediyoruz. Ancak iş hayatta kalma mücadelesine ve evlatlarını korumaya geldiğinde, o karakterlerin birer savaşçıya dönüşmesi, ellerine geçen her şeyle bu canavarlara karşı direniş göstermesi çok daha gerçekçi ve tatmin ediciydi. ----------------------------------------------------------- Üstelik 2024 yapımında James McAvoy'un sergilediği narsist ve manipülatif delilik performansı, orijinal filmdeki Patrick karakterine kıyasla ekrandaki tehdit unsurunu çok daha devasa bir boyuta ulaştırmış. The dialogue was bad for the most part, but I could have turned a blind eye to that if the characters hadn't been written as the world's ultimate idiots. On top of that, these "unexpected" villains had zero motivation for what they were doing, nor did they have anything interesting added to their backgrounds. Not to be a big bad wolf all of the time, I'll say that the film does have some merit; there are a few intriguing scenes and couple of note-worthy filmmaking choices... I think knowing exactly where the story was going inevitably changed the experience for me, especially because so much of the film’s effectiveness comes from gradually realising that something is deeply wrong with this seemingly ordinary couple. Even knowing the destination, though, I thought the original handled that progression much better. It takes its time letting the discomfort build, with little moments that initially seem harmless becoming increasingly sinister. The social awkwardness is painful in the best way. Every meal, conversation and attempt at politeness feels like a negotiation where everyone knows something is wrong but nobody wants to be the person who actually says it. That aspect of the film worked really well for me. Speak No Evil understands how horrifying it can be to find yourself trapped in a social situation where basic manners start working against your survival instincts. The parents are constantly making excuses for behaviour that should immediately set off alarm bells, partly because they don’t want to appear rude, and that makes the whole thing so uncomfortable to watch. But their survival instincts made me so frustrated. There is nothing that takes me out of the immersion in a horror film quicker than watching characters voluntarily walk back into a situation they already know is dangerous. These people have so many opportunities to do something. Run. Fight. Make a scene. Literally anything. Instead, they repeatedly return to the same nightmare. I understand the film is deliberately exploring passivity, but I wasn't frightened for them. I was angry at them. The parents are spineless. And even though Agnes is just a kid, I hate her and her stupid bunny. I also think knowing the ending from the remake made some of this even more frustrating. I wasn’t experiencing the mystery in the same way someone going in completely blind would. I knew what the couple were capable of, so I spent a lot of the runtime waiting for the parents to realise what was obvious to me. That probably made their decisions feel even more ridiculous. Still, I prefer this version. It feels much more interested in letting the dread accumulate rather than rushing towards conventional horror beats. It’s not constantly trying to scare you. The story feels nastier and more hopeless, and the whole premise becomes less about a conventional monster and more about the consequences of refusing to trust your own instincts. I definitely think I would have experienced this differently if I’d seen it first. I probably spent too much of the film comparing the two in my head. But even with that handicap, Speak No Evil captures the feeling of being trapped in a deeply uncomfortable social situation and slowly realising that you're in danger so well. 5.6/10

The whole “Yes, yes… let’s turn around just to get some stupid stuffed animal” moment isn’t just bad decision making, it’s the thesis of the entire movie. It’s tense, it’s uncomfortable, it’s bleak. But it’s also infuriating, because you’re stuck watching a dad who would rather die than be rude. And honestly? That’s the real horror…

On a vacation in Toscana, a Danish family instantly becomes friends with a Dutch family. Months later, the Danish couple receives an unexpected invitation. It doesn't take long before the joy of reunion is replaced with misunderstandings. Because it’s labeled as a horror movie and because it took me a few years to watch it so I was aware of its reputation going in, Speak No Evil is an exercise in tension and dread, since you’re just waiting for something bad to happen. A father (Morten Burian), a mother (Sidsel Siem Koch) and their young daughter (Liva Forsberg) are vacationing in Tuscany. At their villa, this Danish clan meet another family of three. That trio’s patriarch (Fedja van Huêt) couldn’t be more gregarious; his wife (Karina Smulders) seems equally as friendly and outgoing. Their son, curiously, says nothing — the parents explain he suffers from a birth defect that’s affected his tongue. A few months later, the Danes are invited to visit their new friends at their house deep in the woods, where there’s no phone reception and no one to call for help. The gathering becomes increasingly uncomfortable as polite disagree-ments and cultural misunderstandings devolve into something far more sinister. And with that simple premise, filmmaker Christian Tafdrup sets up a middle-class descent into hell. Speak No Evil is all about the masks we put on in public and how we let minor offenses slide in the name of being friendly and polite. With claustro-phobic direction from Tafdrup and a clever, cruel script by his brother Mads, the movie is a very uncomfortable experience of increasing tension. Little by little, the family’s vacation becomes more sinister, but the changes occur so slowly that they only realize the full extent of the horrors they’ll meet when it’s too late. The movie lays bare the idea that not everyone is kind, not everyone is good, and some of those people are fine with being monsters. Further still, some of them win . Speak No Evil also has one of the bleakest endings in the history of cinema that’s guaranteed to make you cancel your next trip, or at least make you think twice about who you make friends with. Great performances from the entire cast too.

Concordamos com um motorista de Uber falando besteira apenas para não gastar energia discutindo, nos colocamos em situações desconfortáveis para não parecermos rígidos demais, flexibilizamos momentaneamente nossos próprios valores para não sermos vistos como chatos ou mal-educados. Speak No Evil pega algo absolutamente cotidiano e apenas o extrapola até transformá-lo em um terror desconfortável. Assistimos aos protagonistas caminharem lentamente em direção ao abismo. E o mais angustiante é perceber que não existe uma grande decisão responsável por levá-los até lá. São pequenas concessões, uma após a outra. Para não provocar desconforto, tornam-se progressivamente mais permissivos, até o momento em que aquilo que poderia ter sido evitado parece inevitável. No fim, Speak No Evil talvez seja um terror comportamental antes de qualquer outra coisa. Não precisa investir em jump scares, ameaças sobrenaturais ou grandes estímulos visuais. Seu terror está no comportamento humano e da facilidade com que reconhecemos aquelas pequenas concessões em nós mesmos. O filme apenas leva às últimas consequências uma armadilha na qual entramos todos os dias: o medo de contrariar o próximo.

A huge number of reactions to Speak No Evil boil down to: “I would simply have behaved rationally and escaped.” Yes. Congratulations. You defeated the movie while sitting on your couch. Christian Tafdrup's film is vicious because every individual act of submission is just small enough to rationalize. Stay a little longer. Don't make a scene. Accept the strange behavior. Retrieve the stuffed rabbit. Ignore the boundary violation because objecting would create an awkward social moment. The entire film is about how catastrophe can be assembled out of manners. That makes the constant complaint that the protagonists are “too passive” particularly funny. Their passivity is the fucking subject. Tafdrup exaggerates it into nightmare logic, but the mechanism is recognizable: people routinely endure astonishing amounts of discomfort because they do not want to become the person who openly says, “No, this is weird and I am leaving.” The villains understand this perfectly. Their real weapon is not physical strength. It is social permission. The film eventually becomes so cruel that it risks collapsing into misanthropic comedy, and I think that is intentional. By the final stretch, Tafdrup is no longer asking how much politeness can cost. He is staging an execution of liberal civility. “Because you let me” is almost too neat a thesis statement, but it lands because the entire film has already demonstrated it in increasingly ridiculous increments. People call the ending unrealistic. Maybe. But horror has always exaggerated ordinary weaknesses until they become fatal. Usually the weakness is curiosity, greed, lust, arrogance. Here it is being the kind of person who would rather die than make dinner awkward.
